evidence.tested: Retrospective satellite classification and temporal transfer to 2019–2021 imagery; mapped class proportions compared across years.
evidence.unknown: No direct geohazard outcomes or causal attribution; one highway region and reference-label uncertainty limit transfer.

summary: Random Forest classification of fused Sentinel optical and radar observations mapped land-cover change along a section of India’s National Highway 344 from 2016 to 2021. Tall vegetation decreased from 32.73% of the mapped area in 2016 to 24.02% in 2018, with partial later recovery; urban cover increased. Feature selection yielded reported classification accuracy of 92.75%. These are retrospective land-cover estimates, not measured erosion, landslide or flood outcomes, and the study does not isolate a causal highway effect.
title: Satellite machine learning maps vegetation change near a highway
